name: Fipsen
summary: North German trick-taking auction game where one declarer bids tricks and plays solo against three opponents.
rules_text: Prisdorf variant: 4 players use 25 cards - a Skat pack with all Diamonds removed except the 7 of Diamonds, which is the preference suit. Rank is natural Ace high, 7 low. Deal 5 cards each in 3+2, with a 2-card skat laid after first packet and 3 cards aside for Kieker. Auction clockwise from forehand. Bids are 2 to 5 tricks. A Hand bid means no skat and beats same number; Ruten declares Diamonds trump (only one diamond) and doubles value. Bidding starts at 2; a player can hold a higher bid. Player with no courts (Jack/Queen/King) may bid Kieker between 4 and 5, picking up skat+stock (10 cards) and discarding 5 before declaring trump. Four 7s plus Ace is Siebener Fips, wins 30 unplayed. Declarer (except Hand/Kieker) picks up skat, discards 2, announces trump. Must follow suit if able. If declarer makes bid he scores bid value doubled for Hand and/or Ruten; fails loses double. Taking all 5 is Durch and doubles again.
rating_reason: North German trick-taking, 4-5 players, playable strategy.
